source.title: Deep Learning: Generalization Requires Deep Compositional Feature Space Design

record.file_problem: Full paper text supplied; no apparent truncation or garbling that prevents extraction.
record.tranche_reason: The paper reports CIFAR-10 validation/test accuracy with dropout enabled and disabled, testing whether dropout lowers test error. Its other experiments concern convolutional feature-space design and learning-rate decay, not the specific versioned claims.
record.gate_note: The paper cites Zhang et al. and other prior work, but those cited findings are not rows. Its results do not test random-label memorization, fully connected versus convolutional networks, or the other versioned comparisons. Tables I, II, IV, V and VI report additional CIFAR-10 architecture or learning-rate results that do not match a listed version; they are recorded under fits_no_version.
record.test_reason: The study tests V6 in a new CIFAR-10 convolutional architecture through a dropout ablation with batch normalization held constant. It is not an original source for V6.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors attribute better generalization to compositional feature-space design combined with explicit and implicit regularization, characterize learning-rate decay as an implicit regularizer, and argue for an optimal architecture and parameter count. Their concluding claim extends to any dataset, although their experiments cover only CIFAR-10.
record.recipe_differences: The paper evaluates dropout in a CIFAR-10 convolutional classifier; it does not state enough detail to establish a direct reproduction of the cited dropout study's setup.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported test accuracy varies across architecture designs, downsampling method, learning-rate policy, first-layer stride, depth, dropout, and batch-normalization settings.

fits_no_version.finding: Designs 1, 2 and 3 achieve 89.4%, 86.8% and 87.9% accuracy at similar parameter counts.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Convolutional composition and spatial downsampling choices affect CIFAR-10 accuracy at similar parameter counts.

fits_no_version.finding: Strided convolution achieves 91.7% accuracy versus 89.4% with max pooling.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The tested strided-convolution design outperforms its max-pooling comparator.

fits_no_version.finding: With dropout present, accuracy is 91.7% with batch normalization and 88.2% without.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Batch normalization improves accuracy in the tested dropout-equipped convolutional classifier.

fits_no_version.finding: Polynomial decay achieves 91.7% accuracy versus 90.1% with step decay.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Learning-rate decay policy affects accuracy in the tested architecture.

fits_no_version.finding: Moving stride to the first convolution lowers accuracy from 91.7% to 89.4%.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The location of spatial downsampling affects accuracy in the tested architecture.

fits_no_version.finding: The deeper design 4 achieves 89.3% accuracy versus design 1 conv's 91.7%.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Increasing depth with the tested architectural changes does not improve accuracy.

record.problems: The results report test accuracy without uncertainty estimates. The dropout comparison covers only a single CIFAR-10 design; the reported dropout/no-dropout contrast is modest and does not test multiple training-set sizes or dropout strengths.
record.rows_left_out: No reported result rows were omitted. Table III's duplicate dropout-plus-batch-normalization result is represented once as R6, which also records its direct comparison to the no-dropout condition.

untested.parts: No own experiments comparing random-label memorization and natural-label generalization.
No width sweep or identification of the width needed for zero training error.
No convolutional versus fully connected comparison.
No adaptive optimizer versus SGD comparison or tuning-budget experiment.

Fully connected classifiers, very small training sets, excessive dropout, and joint removal of dropout and weight decay under augmentation are untested. Dropout without batch normalization lacks a matched no-dropout control.
No magnitude-aware sharpness measurements or comparisons of generalization-gap rankings.
No memorization-based example removal and retraining.

record.verdict_notes: Table III's supplied text clearly identifies the three conditions and accuracies. No uncertainty estimates or repeated-run results are reported. The comparison between decay policies establishes a performance difference, but does not independently establish the proposed regularization mechanism.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label fit and held-out performance on natural labels are discussed or cited, not experimentally tested.
No width sweep beyond the interpolation threshold.
No comparison with fully connected networks or test of local connectivity's contribution.
No adaptive optimizer versus SGD comparison.
The experiments report one CIFAR-10 model design and do not test very small training sets, too much dropout, or removing dropout and weight decay together with data augmentation.
No magnitude-aware sharpness or other generalization-gap measure.
No removal and retraining of memorized examples.

relationships.condition: CIFAR-10, design 1 conv, batch normalization enabled, with data augmentation
relationships.reason: R6 reports 91.7% accuracy with dropout versus 90.1% without, reducing test error by 1.6 percentage points. This supports dropout's benefit in this regime; untested regimes do not warrant limits_scope.
relationships.display_finding: The study reports higher test accuracy with dropout, but this comparison remains unverified.
